The O3 frontend formats dates through `formatDate` in the esm-core framework. It reads the user's locale from i18next, uses `Intl` for the output, and replaces today's date with a localized "Today".

**How it works**

1. **Locale:** `getLocale()` returns `window.i18next.language`, normalized to a BCP 47 tag, with a special case that maps `ht` to `fr-HT` @file:{github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-core::packages/framework/esm-utils/src/get-locale.ts:7-18}.
2. **Defaults:** `formatDate` defaults to `mode: 'standard'`, `time: 'for today'`, and `day`/`month`/`year` on, with `noToday: false`. Amharic (`am`) turns `noToday` on by default @file:{github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-core::packages/framework/esm-utils/src/dates/date-util.ts:208-215}.
3. **Today check:** `formatDate` uses dayjs's `isToday` plugin. If the date is today and `noToday` is false, it returns `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat(locale, { numeric: 'auto' }).format(0, 'day')`, with the first letter uppercased. That is where "Today" comes from in each language @file:{github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-core::packages/framework/esm-utils/src/dates/date-util.ts:306-332}.
4. **Other dates:** the code builds `Intl.DateTimeFormat` options (`year: 'numeric'`, `month: 'short'`, `day: '2-digit'`, plus an optional calendar and numbering system). For English it switches the locale to `en-GB` so the output is day-month-year, and for English and Amharic in standard mode it joins parts with hyphens. Wide mode joins them with " — " @file:{github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-core::packages/framework/esm-utils/src/dates/date-util.ts:318-350}.
5. **Time:** for today, with the default `'for today'` setting, `formatDate` appends `, <time>`. `time: true` always appends it. `formatTime` uses `toLocaleTimeString` with 2-digit hour and minute, so the 12- or 24-hour clock follows the locale @file:{github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-core::packages/framework/esm-utils/src/dates/date-util.ts:366-370}, @file:{github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-core::packages/framework/esm-utils/src/dates/date-util.ts:396-401}.
6. **Other entry points:** `formatDatetime` is `formatDate` with `time: true` @file:{github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-core::packages/framework/esm-utils/src/dates/date-util.ts:416-418}. `formatPartialDate` parses partial strings such as "2000-01" in the current locale, hides the missing parts, and delegates to `formatDate` @file:{github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-core::packages/framework/esm-utils/src/dates/date-util.ts:241-280}.

**Documentation**

- The O3 docs recipe `content/en-US/docs/recipes/format-dates.mdx` describes `formatDate` (lines 7–30). It says the default is `time: "for today"` and that today is shown as `Today`, with `{ time: false }` and `{ noToday: true }` as the overrides @file:{github.com/openmrs/openmrs-contrib-o3-docs::content/en-US/docs/recipes/format-dates.mdx:7-30}. It also covers `formatDatetime` (lines 58–80), `formatTime` (lines 83–99), and `isOmrsDateToday` (line 136).
- The French version (`content/fr-FR/docs/recipes/format-dates.mdx`) says the same thing.

**Tests**

- The English "Today" output and the `noToday` behaviour are tested at @file:{github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-core::packages/framework/esm-utils/src/dates/date-util.test.ts:54-66}, @file:{github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-core::packages/framework/esm-utils/src/dates/date-util.test.ts:154-160}, and @file:{github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-core::packages/framework/esm-utils/src/dates/date-util.test.ts:183-202}. The tests cover Russian, French ("Aujourd'hui"), Amharic, and Thai date output.

**Not verified**

- The docs mention calendar registration (`registerDefaultCalendar`, `getDefaultCalendar`, and the `preferredCalendar` styleguide setting). I did not read those implementations, so I can't say how calendars are chosen.
- I did not check how the patient chart repo calls these functions.

The three patient chart components that use `WarningIcon` are all order-basket item tiles, and each renders it only when an order error is present. Nothing in the chart uses `AllergiesIcon`, which is an alias of `WarningIcon` in the framework, so no alias-based usage needs checking.

1. **Medications order basket** renders the icon beside the order error text. It is imported from `@openmrs/esm-framework` and used at `<WarningIcon size={16} />` inside the `orderError` block: @file:{openmrs-esm-patient-chart::packages/esm-patient-medications-app/src/drug-order-basket-panel/order-basket-item-tile.component.tsx:5-5} and @file:{openmrs-esm-patient-chart::packages/esm-patient-medications-app/src/drug-order-basket-panel/order-basket-item-tile.component.tsx:87-96}.

2. **Lab tests order basket** uses it the same way for lab order errors: @file:{openmrs-esm-patient-chart::packages/esm-patient-tests-app/src/test-orders/lab-order-basket-panel/lab-order-basket-item-tile.component.tsx:5-5} and @file:{openmrs-esm-patient-chart::packages/esm-patient-tests-app/src/test-orders/lab-order-basket-panel/lab-order-basket-item-tile.component.tsx:42-52}.

3. **General order basket** (`esm-patient-orders-app`) uses it for generic order errors: @file:{openmrs-esm-patient-chart::packages/esm-patient-orders-app/src/order-basket/general-order-type/order-basket-item-tile.component.tsx:5-5} and @file:{openmrs-esm-patient-chart::packages/esm-patient-orders-app/src/order-basket/general-order-type/order-basket-item-tile.component.tsx:34-44}.

The icon is defined in the framework at @file:{openmrs-esm-core::packages/framework/esm-styleguide/src/icons/icons.tsx:848-859}, and its mocks are at @file:{openmrs-esm-core::packages/framework/esm-styleguide/mock.tsx:103-103} and @file:{openmrs-esm-core::packages/framework/esm-styleguide/mock-jest.tsx:102-102}. Those mocks only affect tests, not runtime behaviour.

Scope and limits: I only grepped the patient chart checkout locally and searched `openmrs-esm-core` through Falkon. I did not search the other repositories, so consumers outside the patient chart (the date picker and login app in core, for example) are not covered here. Falkon's repository-scoped grep failed with the short names, so I used the full `github.com/openmrs/...` name for the core search. The patient chart search was local, not through Falkon.

Possible effects in the patient chart: a behaviour change to the icon's size, markup, or accessibility would show up in these three error states. Snapshot or unit tests that match the icon's output may also need updating.

**Flow for adding a visit attribute to an existing visit**

1. **Frontend request:** `createVisitAttribute(visitUuid, attributeType, value)` POSTs `{ attributeType, value }` to `${restBaseUrl}/visit/${visitUuid}/attribute` (@file:{openmrs-esm-patient-chart::packages/esm-patient-chart-app/src/visit/visit-form/visit-form.resource.ts:172-178}). The save workspace calls it for new attributes at @file:{openmrs-esm-patient-chart::packages/esm-patient-chart-app/src/visit/visit-form/exported-visit-form.workspace.tsx:249}. Edits to existing attributes use `updateVisitAttribute` (@file:{openmrs-esm-patient-chart::packages/esm-patient-chart-app/src/visit/visit-form/visit-form.resource.ts:180-186}), called at line 217 of the same workspace file.

2. **Server REST handler:** `VisitAttributeResource1_9` is a sub-resource at path `attribute` under `VisitResource1_9`. Its `save` sets the attribute on the visit (via `setAttribute` when max occurs is 1, otherwise `addAttribute`) and then calls `Context.getVisitService().saveVisit(visit)` (@file:{openmrs-module-webservices.rest::omod/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/resource/openmrs1_9/VisitAttributeResource1_9.java:29-31}, @file:{openmrs-module-webservices.rest::omod/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/resource/openmrs1_9/VisitAttributeResource1_9.java:97-116}). I did not open `BaseAttributeCrudResource1_9` to confirm how the generic controller dispatches a POST to `save`.

3. **Core service:** `VisitServiceImpl.saveVisit` checks the ADD_VISITS or EDIT_VISITS privilege, calls `CustomDatatypeUtil.saveAttributesIfNecessary(visit)`, then delegates to `dao.saveVisit` (@file:{openmrs-core::api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/impl/VisitServiceImpl.java:178-187}).

4. **Data access:** `HibernateVisitDAO.saveVisit` runs `HibernateUtil.saveOrUpdate(getCurrentSession(), visit)`, which is the database write (@file:{openmrs-core::api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/db/hibernate/HibernateVisitDAO.java:165-169}). The DAO interface declaration is at @file:{openmrs-core::api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/db/VisitDAO.java:86}.

Not verified: the `VisitService` interface declaration of `saveVisit`, `CustomDatatypeUtil.saveAttributesIfNecessary`, and the generic base class `BaseAttributeCrudResource1_9`. These are the remaining links I did not open.

The delete path runs from the chart's confirmation modal through the REST client, the webservices.rest sub-resource controller and allergy resource, and into openmrs-core's `PatientService` and Hibernate DAO. The allergy is soft-deleted, not removed: the code sets `voided` and `voidReason` and then persists the row.

1. **Frontend trigger:** the "Delete" button in the modal calls `handleDelete`, which calls `deletePatientAllergy` and then revalidates the allergy list. @file:{openmrs-esm-patient-chart::packages/esm-patient-allergies-app/src/allergies/delete-allergy.modal.tsx:18-46}
2. **Frontend request:** `deletePatientAllergy` sends `DELETE {restBaseUrl}/patient/{patientUuid}/allergy/{allergyUuid}`. @file:{openmrs-esm-patient-chart::packages/esm-patient-allergies-app/src/allergies/allergy-intolerance.resource.ts:89-94}
3. **REST route:** the generic sub-resource controller matches `/{resource}/{parentUuid}/{subResource}/{uuid}` with `DELETE` and no `purge` parameter. It looks up the `patient/allergy` sub-resource and calls `delete(parentUuid, uuid, reason, context)`. @file:{openmrs-module-webservices.rest::omod-common/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/controller/MainSubResourceController.java:158-169}
4. **REST handler:** `PatientAllergyResource2_0` looks up the allergy by UUID, throws `ObjectNotFoundException` if it is missing, and calls `voidAllergy`. @file:{openmrs-module-webservices.rest::omod/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/resource/openmrs2_0/PatientAllergyResource2_0.java:210-219}. The single-argument `delete(Allergy, ...)` at lines 197-200 is the same call without the parent lookup.
5. **Core service:** `PatientServiceImpl.voidAllergy(Allergy, String)` sets `voided`, `voidedBy`, `dateVoided` and `voidReason`, then calls `dao.saveAllergy`. @file:{openmrs-core::api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/impl/PatientServiceImpl.java:1581-1589}. The interface declaration is at @file:{openmrs-core::api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/PatientService.java:992}.
6. **Data access:** `HibernatePatientDAO.saveAllergy` calls `sessionFactory.getCurrentSession().persist(allergy)`. This is the database write, though the UPDATE is flushed later by the Hibernate session. @file:{openmrs-core::api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/db/hibernate/HibernatePatientDAO.java:1009-1013}. The DAO interface is at @file:{openmrs-core::api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/db/PatientDAO.java:299}.

Other paths I did not follow:
- `PatientServiceImpl.removeAllergy` (lines 1573-1576) also calls `voidAllergy`, but I found no caller for it in the REST path.
- The "delete all allergies" branch of the handler (lines 219-226) is not used by the modal.
- `allergies-action-menu.component.tsx` opens the modal; I did not trace it.
- I did not check whether the REST module's own `patient/allergy` resource is registered under another name.

`reportError` is used in two places in the patient chart, and both are error-reporting hooks. Each only runs when an error occurs, so a change in `reportError`'s behaviour would show up there, but nothing else in the chart calls it.

**What `reportError` does now.** It normalises the value with `ensureErrorObject` and rethrows it inside `setTimeout`, so the error surfaces as an uncaught global error (`window.onerror`) rather than being handled inline. @file:{github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-core::packages/framework/esm-error-handling/src/index.ts:56-61}

**Chart call sites, most affected first:**

1. **`useOrderableConceptSWR`** calls `reportError(error)` in a `useEffect` whenever the SWR fetch fails. It has no dependency array, so it runs on every render while `error` is set. @file:{github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-patient-chart::packages/esm-patient-common-lib/src/orders/useOrderableConceptSets.ts:23-61}, call at line 36.

2. **`useOrderableConceptSets`** is the public hook built on that SWR call. It calls `reportError(error)` in a second `useEffect` keyed on `[error]`. @file:{github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-patient-chart::packages/esm-patient-common-lib/src/orders/useOrderableConceptSets.ts:65-91}, call at line 73. It is the hook the orders UI consumes, so it is the main place where a change would reach users.

3. **`useFavoritesActions` → `persistFavorites`** calls `reportError(error)` in the `catch` block when saving drug favourites fails, then shows an error snackbar. @file:{github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-patient-chart::packages/esm-patient-orders-app/src/order-favorites/useFavoritesActions.ts:18-108}, with the call at line 57 inside `persistFavorites` at @file:{github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-patient-chart::packages/esm-patient-orders-app/src/order-favorites/useFavoritesActions.ts:25-68}.

**Mocks.** The framework's own test mocks also declare `reportError` (for example @file:{github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-core::packages/framework/esm-framework/mock.tsx:52-55} and @file:{github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-core::packages/framework/esm-framework/mock-jest.tsx:51-54}). If the signature or semantics change, these would need matching updates for chart tests that rely on them, but they are not runtime code.

**Limits.** The chart grep and the symbol-reference lookup both returned the same two files, so I found no other direct uses. I did not check whether `reportError` is re-exported through `@openmrs/esm-framework` in a way that would hide a call, and I did not check the other 40+ OpenMRS repositories. I also did not look at whether the chart's tests assert on `reportError` calls beyond the mock definitions.
